body:
Actually the situation with `RichTextLabel` is a bit different and inconsistent with `Label`, but still broken for the core repro case above. (Note that these classes do not share any relevant code internally.)

Unlike `Label`, `RichTextLabel` never updates its `visible_ratio` when the text changes, instead keeping `visible_characters` as the "source of truth". But still, when you change the text, and then attempt to set `visible_ratio` to the same value it already has, it will not work. So the repro steps for `RichTextLabel` are as follows:

1. Have a `RichTextLabel` with `text = "Short text"` (len=10).
2. Set `visible_characters = 10`, the exact length of the text. (This sets `visible_ratio` to 1.0.)
3. Set `text` to a new, longer string, `"Very long text, so so long"` (len=26). (The text is truncated as "Very long " though in this case, it is not inconsisteny behaviour with shorter values. However, `visible_ratio` erroneously remains at 1.0 even though it **should** be set to 0.38.)
4. Set `visible_ratio = 1.0`. This has no effect, and the text remains truncated.

In this case, you can repro this with any value of `visible_ratio`. For example, set `visible_characters` to 6 (causing `visible_ratio` to become 0.6), switch to long text, then setting `visible_ratio` to 0.6 has no effect).

I am working on a fix for this (I've got `Label` fixed already) but now that I have discovered the inconsistent behaviour with `RichTextLabel`, it's unclear whether the fix should be to change the overall behaviour of `RichTextLabel` to match `Label`, or keep it the way it is but just fix up `visible_ratio`. For now I will opt for the latter. Filed a separate bug #119840 to discuss specifically whether to make `RichTextLabel` consistent with `Label`.
